item.title: The 76ers jump to betting favorite out East after LeBron James takes his talents to Philadelphia
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers jumped past the New York Knicks as Eastern Conference betting favorites after signing LeBron James to a two-year, $8 million deal.
item.content:encoded:
Love him or hate him, LeBron James is still a needle-mover. At least in the sportsbooks and prediction markets.

After signing LeBron to a team-friendly two-year, $8 million deal, the Philadelphia 76ers are now the betting favorite in the Eastern Conference to win the 2027 championship at Kalshi.

I know the percentages can be confusing, so in American odds, the Sixers are +684 to win the title next season. They passed the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks, who are the second-betting favorite (+1240) out East as of 2 p.m. ET Friday, July 24.

LEBRON JAMES MAKES NBA FREE AGENCY DECISION, ANNOUNCES PLANS TO SIGN WITH 76ERS

This is the second huge move Philly has made this offseason, coming off the heels of trading Paul George to the Boston Celtics for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown.

Now, Philadelphia's starting five includes LeBron, Brown, 2022-23 NBA MVP Joel Embiid, two-time All-Star guard Tyrese Maxey, and SG V.J. Edgecombe, who finished third in Rookie of the Year voting last season.

Ultimately, the question: Is this team good enough to win a title?

I mean, if the 76ers get insane injury luck in the playoffs, of course they can win a championship. Every team can. And in an NBA2K-sense: Sure. If you turn off injuries and control the players yourself.

Whether the personalities and playing styles mesh is another conversation. In fact, there's a solid chance the 2026-27 Philadelphia 76ers will be a too many cooks in the kitchen type thing.

In theory, upgrading from PG to Brown, while adding LeBron to a Sixers squad that upset the Celtics in the first round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs (which led Boston to spazz and make a franchise-altering trade), is a power move.

CELTICS AGREE TO SEND JAYLEN BROWN, 2024 FINALS MVP, TO 76ERS IN BLOCKBUSTER NBA TRADE: REPORT

Brown is a champion and five-time NBA All-Star who averaged career-bests in points, rebounds and assists last season. He is in his athletic prime and has never suffered a significant injury.

Again, love him or hate him, LeBron balled last season, his final with the Los Angeles Lakers. He averaged 20.9 points on 51.5% shooting with 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists in 60 games.

But LeBron has always been ball-dominant, and I don't see him changing much at 41, soon-to-be 42-years-old. Brown is an iso-scorer who likes to take defenders off the dribble and operates in the mid-range.

Philadelphia needs Embiid healthy and playing at 70% of his MVP-self to justify being the betting favorite in the East. However, Embiid always gets hurt, and he is a much worse defender than he was when in his prime.

Maxey actually led the 76ers in scoring last season despite Embiid having the highest usage rate on the team. Are we sure he'll be okay with giving the ball up to LeBron and Brown?

Deferring isn't the same as buying into a lesser role and still playing your a-- off. It isn't guaranteed that two or three All-Stars will be cool with being essentially role players, and you need "glue guys" to win a title.

That said, Philly should be second to New York as the betting favorite to win the East. The Knicks will have the same starting five in their title defense, all of whom are in their athletic primes. If they met in the playoffs, Jalen Brunson would be the best player on the floor.

_____________________________

Follow me on X @Geoffery-Clark, and check out my "OutKick Bets Podcast" for more betting content and random rants.

item.title: Paul Anka slams modern singers, says Frank Sinatra would have 'thrown a chair'
item.description: Paul Anka says Frank Sinatra would have thrown a chair if asked to use autotune, praising an era when singers had to perform live until perfect.
item.content:encoded:
Paul Anka slammed modern singers and the technology that helps them sound better, saying Franka Sinatra would have thrown a chair at someone if they asked him to use autotune.

Anka called Sinatra and Elvis Presley his two "towers" of music while speaking to Billy Corgan of the Smashing Pumpkins on his "The Magnificent Others" podcast this week.

"When Elvis was around, he just – they both owned a room, and they were both given that it factor," he explained.

FRANK SINATRA'S DESERT HIDEAWAY WAS 'ALL SEX, ALL THE TIME,' FORMER VALET CLAIMS

He added, "And Elvis worked his a-- off. This was a shy guy. I would sit with him like this: ‘Hey, Paulie,’" he said in a reserved imitation of Presley. "‘How you doing, man? Yeah, Paul. You know, one day I'm going to do that "My Way." I love that "My Way."’"

He said he told Presley that he wouldn’t want to cover the song made famous by Sinatra because it wasn’t exactly his style of music.

"But what an amazing force to watch and be around it," he continued.

The "Put Your Head on My Shoulder" singer said he and Presley learned that it "wasn't about just getting up there and singing. You had to entertain people."

The 84-year-old gave the example of the notoriously unpredictable Bob Dylan, whom he admits he loves, but said would sometimes go on stage and "couldn’t give a s--- and people walk out, ‘What the f---?’ If you don't entertain people, you're dead."

Regarding Sinatra, he vowed the "Fly Me to the Moon" crooner "will get bigger, young people will learn exactly what true quality is, you know, at a time when there was no autotune."

"Think about the difference. I don't know who the f--- is doing the singing today. Do you?" he admitted. "Can you imagine back then if you said to Sinatra, ‘We're going to give you an autotune’? He would have thrown a chair at you."

Singers in Sinatra’s time, he said, "walked in a studio after rehearsing, as I stated earlier, and you kept singing, and that band kept playing till you got perfect."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"That was it," he continued. "And he was the guy."

Anka said Sinatra set the standard and "made it tough for anybody to ever stand in front of a band again. We all came second, but he was the guy we emulated."

He also said that Sammy Davis, Jr. was the most "short-changed" on being recognized.

"To Frank and Dean [Martin] and to all of us, he was the most talented," Anka said.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"That was the most talented guy," he professed. "He was a musician. He played drums. He played this, he did that. He sang great. He was the guy that I hope today somehow they put him back in the forefront. And Dean was an underrated singer."

Anka said a specific song that he wrote for Davis but didn't name was "as important to me as ‘My Way’ with Sinatra."

Anka wrote "My Way" for Sinatra in 1968.

He also praised Michael Jackson’s talent, saying, "I never worked with anyone like that … I knew the kid was so talented."

item.title: Man accused of raping three underage girls faces new charge from prison
item.description: Imarr Finley, facing rape charges involving three underage girls in Harrisburg, now faces vandalism charges after allegedly breaking a Dauphin County Prison window.
item.content:encoded:
A man awaiting trial for allegedly raping three underage girls is facing new charges after reportedly breaking a window inside a Pennsylvania prison.

Imarr Finley, 25, of Harrisburg, Pa., has been at the jail since December 2024, when he was arrested after allegedly kidnapping a 12-year-old girl on her way home from school, taking her to his home and raping her, according to court records obtained by Pennlive.com.

Court records show Finley was charged with the rape of two other girls. One girl was 17, while the other was 13 or 14, Pennlive.com reported.

Finley's most recent criminal charge stems from a July 8 incident when he allegedly broke a control room window on the Dauphin County Prison's P block while he was out of his cell on recreation time, according to a probable cause affidavit obtained by Pennlive.com.

FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES

The affidavit, filed by the Dauphin County District Attorney’s Office, claimed two corrections officers saw Finley break the window, which caused $772 in damage.

Court records show Finley was charged on Thursday with institutional vandalism, a second-degree misdemeanor.

For that charge, he was arraigned on Thursday afternoon and a preliminary hearing has been scheduled for Aug. 4. Fox News Digital reached out to the prison for comment.

The first alleged rape occurred on Nov. 25, 2024, in the uptown Harrisburg area, according to police.

According to Pennlive.com, the girl told authorities that a man dressed in all black and a mask over his face was following her.

FORMER PRISON GUARD WHO HAD SEX TAPE WITH INMATE GO VIRAL IS FILLED WITH REGRET & NOW FOCUSING ON BEING A MOM

The man, who police say was Finley, got the girl to follow him to his house, where he allegedly raped her and threatened the girl's family if she told anyone, Pennlive.com reported. Days later on Dec. 4, 2024, Finley was arrested by Harrisburg police after he fled out the second story window of a home and tried to flee by running across rooftops, according to authorities.

On March 23, 2026, Finley was charged in connection with the rape of a 13- or 14-year-old girl who he allegedly lured to his house with a fake Snapchat photo, Pennlive.com reported.

Four days later, he was charged with raping a 17-year-old girl after authorities said DNA evidence tied him to the crime, according to the outlet.

Finley is being held without bond and is due to appear in court for the rape charges on July 30.

item.title: Tony Romo arrested in Milwaukee for alleged OWI offense: report

item.content:encoded:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo was arrested in Milwaukee on Thursday night for allegedly operating while intoxicated.

Romo was reportedly stopped on a highway and performed poorly on field sobriety tests, FOX6 in Milwaukee reported. He was released and is due in court Sept. 21.

Romo retired from football in 2017 and soon joined CBS as a color commentator.

item.title: Platner campaign strategist admits tattoo, Reddit posts should have been 'enough' to disqualify him
item.description: Graham Platner strategist Morris Katz said in a new interview that the candidate's Reddit posts and troubling behavior should have disqualified him from the Maine Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
Graham Platner's lead campaign strategist, Morris Katz, admitted on Friday that the controversies that came out about the ex-Maine Democratic Senate candidate early on should have been enough to disqualify him from running.

Katz told The New York Times that the anger and frustration surrounding Platner's campaign was valid. He said he often criticizes establishment Democrats for not learning from their mistakes, and said, "I think there are things here, many of the critiques that have been made, that are incredibly valid and things to learn from."

Platner ended his Senate campaign in July after Jenny Racicot alleged the Senate candidate had raped her when the two were in a relationship in 2021, which was first reported by Politico.

NEW EXPLOSIVE ALLEGATION ROCKS PLATNER CAMPAIGN STILL REELING FROM RAPE ACCUSATION

"That being said, in hindsight, knowing what we know now, the Reddit posts alone probably should have been enough — or should have been enough. The tattoo should have been enough. The initial New York Times story on troubling behavior should have been enough," Katz said.

Katz's remarks drew some derision online, as those who felt Platner was problematic at the time were roundly dismissed and criticized by the candidate's allies.

"What a bunch of arrogant gaslighters," one wrote on X. "Like there were a ton of us who were literally screaming this from the rooftops and were met with all kinds of name-calling."

Platner was flippant about Platner's Nazi tattoo issue in a profile in The New York Times in January. He was quoted as jokingly asking then-Iowa Democratic Senate hopeful Nathan Sage if he had such a tattoo as well.

The New York Times published a story in June highlighting accounts from several women Platner has dated that referenced unsettling behavior. The story faced scrutiny, as another one of Platner's accusers, Lyndsey Fifield, said the paper tainted her account.

Fifield's account was challenged by some left-wing media figures and politicians because of her past working for Republican organizations. She told Fox News Digital she felt betrayed by how the New York Times handled her allegations in the original report Katz referenced.

Klein asked Katz why he once described Platner's Reddit posts as an asset. CNN unearthed Platner's posts in October 2025 and found the Democratic Senate candidate once described himself as a "communist," wrote that "all" police were bastards and argued that many rural White Americans "actually are" racist and unintelligent.

PLATNER’S THREE-DAY VETTING JOB COMES BACK TO HAUNT DEMS AS RAPE ALLEGATION ROCKS SENATE BID

Additional reporting drew scrutiny to other deleted posts, including one in which Platner appeared to downplay concerns about sexual assault. In one post, Platner wrote that people should "take some responsibility for themselves" and avoid becoming so intoxicated that they end up in compromising situations.

Katz said it was good to see people show Platner some grace to show that he could have changed and evolved since the posts.

"I think that was something we needed, and I don’t want to lose that. I don’t want people’s lesson from this to be that there should never be room for grace. I think that there are a lot of people who have made mistakes or said controversial things who we want to win the support of, who we need to earn the trust of. But I also think I was wrong," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Katz said there was a vetting document about Platner and that it did find a Reddit account, but not the extent of what came out throughout the campaign. Klein noted the post about sexual assault and asked Katz about what he thought hearing the comments now.

"I think it should have been a red line. He talked about it being one of the things he regretted saying the most, that it was indicative of a time of his life when he was lost and angry, and that it was in no way reflective of who he was," Katz said.

Maine Democrats are expected to nominate Troy Jackson this weekend to replace Platner as they try to unseat Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, a key swing vote in the Senate. Collins is seeking a sixth term.

Collins has the distinction of being the only Republican U.S. Senator to represent a state that President Donald Trump lost in all three of his presidential races.

item.title: Bombshell memo shows Biden planned to leave Trump with even more massive immigration crisis
item.description: Sen. Eric Schmitt obtained a Biden White House memo revealing plans to expand TPS to over 3.1 million noncitizens in the administration's final days.
item.content:encoded:
A newly-uncovered Biden White House memo from the administration's final days revealed plans that could have expanded Temporary Protected Status (TPS) to more than 3 million noncitizens while acknowledging that previous court challenges had blocked many of President Donald Trump's efforts to end the protections.

TPS is meant for foreign populations experiencing crises like political unrest or natural disasters, and while Trump has tried to end the "temporary" provisions for Haitians, Nepalese, Salvadorans and Sudanese people, lawsuits from pro-migrant advocates have halted most attempts.

"Stakeholders argue that granting TPS will potentially protect many vulnerable people from President-elect Trump's planned mass deportations... They argue that these protections are likely to hold in court, and they are prepared to litigate efforts to terminate or slow down the implementation of TPS for specified nations by the Trump Administration," read a section of the memo — acquired by Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo.

SUPREME COURT WEIGHS TRUMP EFFORT TO TERMINATE TEMPORARY PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIAN, SYRIAN MIGRANTS

"[P]rior federal litigation brought by advocates during the first Trump administration was successful in halting [its] efforts to terminate TPS, though that was due in large part to [its] failure to produce a factual record in support of termination, which is something that could be rectified," the memo went on.

Schmitt said he obtained the memo from Archivist of the United States Edward Forst through his authority as chairman of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on the Constitution.

BIRTH TOURISM COULD SOON CARRY A SEVERE NEW CONSEQUENCE FEW WOULD RISK: 'EXISTENTIAL CRISIS'

"Biden tried to turn TPS into a 3.1-million-person deportation shield, protect Tren de Aragua members, and trap President Trump in years of litigation," he said, adding the move directly betrayed the "will of the people" who ousted liberal Democrats from power the prior election.

"The most disturbing part, Biden's ‘Senior Advisors’ recommended he create 2.1 million NEW TPS designees in the last few weeks of his presidency, despite admitting TPS applications take 6 months," Schmitt added.

"Luckily, that never happened and we have been deporting Ecuadorians and Guatemalans."

TRUMP'S 'THIRD WORLD' TRAVEL BAN COULD BECOME PERMANENT IF FIREBRAND REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER GETS HER WAY

Fox News Digital reached out to Biden, a former Biden official and Schmitt for additional comment.

Schmitt noted that one week after the January 2025 memo — which he said was erroneously dated "2024" — Biden extended TPS protections for nearly 1 million noncitizens, meaning its transmission still led to "a concrete, mass-migration action."

Schmitt shared a clip of his recent floor remarks on a related topic, where he said the U.S. should not be a "get-rich-quick scheme for the third world" and that Americans don’t try to delay enforcement of squatters on their property in real-life.

The memo reminded Biden he gave TPS protections to Afghans, Cameroonians, Ethiopians, people from Burma, Lebanese, Ukrainians and Venezuelan nationals and repeatedly extended protections for Haitians.

"The previous Administration unsuccessfully attempted to terminate TPS designations for Sudan, Nicaragua, Haiti, El Salvador, Nepal, and Honduras. Courts issued preliminary injunctions blocking the Trump Administration's actions," it read. "Your administration took actions to resolve this litigation by either redesignating Haiti or rescinding the terminations."

The memo noted that Trump had said during the 2024 campaign he intended to revoke TPS protections for Haitians and predicted his incoming administration would likely seek to rescind additional TPS designations.

A chart in the memo estimated potential new TPS eligibility for roughly 1.5 million Guatemalans, 600,000 Ecuadorians, 464,000 Nicaraguans, 455,000 Venezuelans, and smaller populations from Ukraine, Sudan, and Afghanistan — figures Schmitt said totaled more than 3.1 million people.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The memo said Biden’s "senior team" had also received requests for varying types of new TPS-related actions before Trump would take office from Sens. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., Catherine Cortez-Masto, D-Nev., Cory Booker, D-N.J., Richard Durbin, D-Ill., Mazie Hirono, D-Hawaii, Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., and Alex Padilla, D-Calif.

"In addition, some stakeholders are requesting that your Administration designate nationals from new countries, most notably Ecuador and Guatemala, for TPS," it stated.

While the proposals outlined in the memo were never fully implemented, the document offers a rare glimpse into the immigration options Biden advisers presented as Trump prepared to return to the White House promising mass deportations.

item.title: Nick Bosa breaks yearslong X hiatus to seemingly celebrate Ryan Clark's ESPN firing
item.description: Nick Bosa broke his four-year silence on X to react to Ryan Clark's ESPN layoff with a single emoji after Clark criticized his MAGA hat in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
After four years off X, Nick Bosa is making up for lost time.

The San Francisco 49ers star edge rusher had not posted on the social media platform since Nov. 12, 2022, aside from just three reposts. That was until Thursday.

The three reposts Bosa had shared included Joe Rogan's 2024 podcast episode with Elon Musk, Michael Bublé promoting a charity, and George Kittle's post from the World Cup final asking for grass instead of turf for NFL stadiums. Ironically, that was the topic of Bosa's last post he wrote himself.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But news that circulated this week was enough for Bosa to get his thumbs going, albeit for an extremely short period of time.

Bosa quoted a post from The Athletic about Ryan Clark being laid off from ESPN, and he made his thoughts relatively clear with just one emoji.

Clark criticized Bosa in the past for wearing a MAGA hat after a game shortly before the 2024 election, which President Donald Trump eventually won.

"It seems very clear to me Nick Bosa understands that when you wear that hat, you take a side," Clark said at the time. "You take a side of division in a sport that’s supposed to bring us together. I’m just waiting for all the people who comment under political and sports things to shut up and dribble or to shut up and play football, to tell him to shut up and rush. But they ain’t going to say it, because they feel the exact same way he do."

Clark recently said that supporting Trump is "more polarizing" than supporting other politicians.

SAQUON BARKLEY 'CAN UNDERSTAND' BACKLASH FOR HIS TRUMP HANGOUT, 'GLAD' GIANTS STARS WORKED OUT DIFFERENCES

"Let’s be honest. Who you supported in 2008, 2012 is nowhere near as polarizing as who you support today," Clark said on his podcast. "[Trump] has clearly picked a side, [and] standing next to him gives the impression that you have to. Which means you stand in direct opposition to the majority of your teammates."

Bosa was fined $11,255 for wearing the hat, but he appeareaed no regrets.

"It was well worth it," Bosa said after the election, before being fined. "I don’t think my position on speaking about it is going to change, so clearly the nation spoke," Bosa added. "We got what we got."

Clark was among several layoffs at the company, including Bart Scott, Tom Pelissero, Karl Ravech, and Cam Newton.

item.title: Panthers defense takes major hit as star pass rusher suffers major injury on first day of camp: reports
item.description: GM Dan Morgan says he's 'sick about it' after the Panthers lost Nic Scourton to a torn ACL, adding to injuries hitting Taylor Moton and Jaycee Horn.
item.content:encoded:
The Carolina Panthers defense suffered a crushing blow on the first day of training camp.

Second-year outside linebacker Nic Scourton tore his ACL during team drills on Thursday, according to multiple reports. The 21-year-old had a strong rookie season and was expected to be a key contributor to the defense.

"I'm just sick about it," Panthers general manager Dan Morgan said Thursday night.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

In 17 games last season, the 2025 second-round draft pick started eight. He recorded 47 tackles, 5.0 sacks and seven tackles for loss.

The Panthers signed star edge rusher Jaelan Phillips in the offseason to a four-year, $120 million contract, with the hopes of pairing him alongside Scourton to form a strong pass-rushing duo.

Scourton will reportedly be placed on injured reserve and will seek a second opinion on the injury.

The former Texas A&M star went down on a wet field late in practice during team drills. Players immediately gathered around him on one knee.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Scourton held his hand over his face as he was led into a waiting cart.

As he was leaving the field, the cart stopped and head coach Dave Canales and every player on the roster individually walked over to hug Scourton before he was taken to the training room.

"They care about each other," Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "Whenever you’re in a group of people doing something hard together, it has a way of creating a special bond. Between all the workouts and going through a full season and an offseason and all that, it means something to the guys. I’m proud of that."

It may be early in training camp, but the Panthers already have been hit hard by injuries to key players.

Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton is out after a blood clot was discovered in his lungs. With left tackle Ickey Ekwonu still recovering from a torn patellar tendon in his knee he suffered in last season's wild-card playoff loss to the Los Angeles Rams, the Panthers will begin the season with both starting tackles on the sideline.

Two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Jaycee Horn is dealing with a foot laceration and did not practice Thursday. Defensive tackles Tershawn Wharton (neck) and Bobby Brown (hamstring) were also out.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Elon Musk fires back at reporter, claims more people 'hate you and the media than you realize'
item.description: Elon Musk told The Economist editor Zanny Minton Beddoes that journalists are more despised than him after she said people loathe the trillionaire's influence.
item.content:encoded:
Elon Musk fired back at The Economist editor-in-chief Zanny Minton Beddoes during a Thursday interview from Tesla's Gigafactory in Texas after she said people loathed him over his efforts to influence European politics.

"I think a lot more people hate you and the media more than you realize," Musk told the journalist.

Beddoes confronted the Tesla and SpaceX CEO after challenging his support for right-wing European political parties and arguing that his wealth, ownership of X and following on the platform gave him unusual power to shape politics abroad.

LIZ PEEK: ELON MUSK’S WELL-DESERVED WIN CAUSES THE ZERO-SUM LEFT TO FREAK OUT

"Why should you be able to shape European politics? You don’t even live there," Beddoes said.

"But do you see why this makes people think that this man who has all this power, he’s the world’s richest man, he thinks he has a right to influence our politics?" Beddoes said. "It’s why people loathe you. I mean, some people do loathe you."

Musk dismissed the criticism by pointing to his roughly 250 million followers on X as evidence that he had more supporters than detractors.

FOX NEWS DOMINATES ON YOUTUBE IN MAY, MORE THAN TRIPLES EVERY BROADCAST NETWORK

"Maybe some people do loathe me, and that’s probably true. I don’t care," Musk said. "But the fact that, as you pointed out, a quarter billion people follow me is that I think a lot more people actually like me than don’t."

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO argued that distrust of the press was greater than opposition to him and asked Beddoes whether she recognized the media's standing with the public.

"Do you realize the media is despised?" Musk said. "Do you realize that journalists, the view of journalists is like, it’s like a favorable view of journalists is like 15%?"

WASHINGTON POST BOASTS IT STARED DOWN ‘UNWARRANTED’ JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SUBPOENA

Beddoes acknowledged that trust in American journalism was low but argued that polarization on social media contributed to the problem.

"I think in part there have been mistakes by journalists and journalism. I totally acknowledge that," Beddoes said. "But I also think that the kind of polarized environment, particularly on social media, fostered by the kinds of things you are pushing on X, actually helps make this worse."

Musk rejected her argument and insisted the public disliked journalists more than him.

"The shoe is on the other foot. They hate you. They hate you far more than they hate me," Musk said. "I think you’re the problem. The media."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The exchange followed a lengthy disagreement about Musk's warnings that Britain could face civil war and his backing of European parties Beddoes described as far right. Musk rejected the label and framed his positions around border security, public safety and government spending.

"I literally said, look, I believe in safe cities, secure borders and sensible spending with respect to government," Musk said. "That doesn’t make me right wing at all in the least."

Musk urged Germans to vote for the Alternative for Germany Party and interviewed its leader, Alice Weidel, on X before Germany's 2025 federal election. He promoted the party in at least two dozen posts over two months, Reuters reported.

Public confidence in the news media has fallen sharply. A 2025 Gallup poll found that 28% of Americans had a great deal or fair amount of trust in newspapers, television and radio to report the news fully, accurately and fairly, a record low.

item.title: Jewish leaders fault Mamdani rhetoric as Upper West Side stabbing, hate crime probe continues
item.description: Jewish leaders in New York City are speaking out against Mayor Zohran Mamdani's rhetoric as an investigation continues into a potential hate crime.
item.content:encoded:
Jewish leaders in New York City are accusing Mayor Zohran Mamdani of "fanning the flames of hatred and division" as an investigation is continuing Friday into a pair of stabbings in Manhattan’s Upper West Side that are being looked at as potential hate crimes.

New York Attorney General Letitia James said both victims in Thursday’s attack are currently in stable condition. The suspect, identified as Raul Morales, 51, is accused of yelling "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing two men on Thursday afternoon, according to officials.

"When the mayor of New York repeatedly uses his platform to relentlessly single out and demonize Israel, the world's only Jewish state, and calls those who support it monsters, he contributes to a climate in which Jewish New Yorkers are increasingly targeted and unsafe," Eric Goldstein, the CEO of the UJA-Federation of New York, said Friday.

"Mayor Mamdani, stop fanning the flames of hatred and division. The consequences are not abstract. They are playing out on our streets. But make no mistake, we're not going anywhere. The Jewish community of New York, the largest in the world outside Israel, will continue to walk the streets of the Upper West Side and all the streets of New York openly and proudly," he added.

SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

Rabbi Yosie Levine of The Jewish Center also said Friday that, "When public officials repeatedly cast the Jewish community as a stand-in for actions of the Israeli government, they create a climate in which Jews become targets."

"You know when I was growing up, the only time we saw security outside of my synagogue or outside of my Jewish day school was when the mayor came to speak. The police were there to protect him. Today, every time the mayor speaks, we need the police to protect us," he added. "Jewish life in America is starting to feel like Jewish life in Europe. Armed guards, bulletproof glass, and the constant fear that yesterday's rhetoric will turn into today's assault."

When asked by Fox News Digital for a response, Mamdani's office highlighted remarks the mayor made to NY1 on Friday, in which he said, "There's no tolerance for antisemitism or hatred of any kind in this city."

"This is a city that believes in the beauty and the breadth of all of its five boroughs and everyone who calls it home. And if anyone is perpetrating this kind of a bigotry, that kind of hatred, they will be held fully accountable," Mamdani told the station.

"When it comes to my comments about Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, they are critiques not based on my personal analysis but rather on objective facts," he added. "They are critiques of a political leader not of people of a specific faith or a religion or a background and my responsibility as the mayor of this city is to keep every New Yorker safe, no matter where they come from, what they believe in, or frankly, even if they agree with my politics. My job is to keep them safe." 

WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS

The victims were identified in media reports as Chok Sung, 57, and Moshe Grunhaus, 50.

"So many people know Moshe, so many people care about him. He was just trying to pray at his synagogue, and now we're the ones praying for his recovery," Levine said. "To have been stabbed 200 feet from the Jewish center evokes all the worst images of the Jewish past. If a Jew can't feel safe walking home from shul in broad daylight on a Thursday afternoon on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, then something has gone profoundly wrong, not only for the Jewish community, but for our city."

Goldstein added that Mamdani's recent video in which he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal" was "political grandstanding."

"This is the largest Jewish community in the world outside of Israel. His words have profound real world consequences on us and shame on him. Shame on him for doing this for perceived political benefit when it has real world consequence for the Jews of New York. He must stop," Goldstein said.

James said after speaking with the NYPD commissioner and local district attorney, "they have asked me not to draw any conclusions as a result of last night's event."

"What I do want to say is that it's really critically important that individuals understand that anti-Semitic acts have been growing in the city of New York. It's really critically important," she said. "And then also acts against the Asian community have also been on the increase. So it's important that I stand with my Jewish friends, that I stand with my Asian friends, that I let everyone know that there should not be any space between any of us, that we should stand together against any form of hate, any act of hate in the city and the state of New York, that it will not be tolerated."

item.title: ‘McCarthy trials’: Hasan Piker, far-left figures erupt over subpoenas in $39M Singham probe
item.description: Hasan Piker and CodePink's Medea Benjamin rally behind BreakThrough News after congressional subpoenas target groups tied to communist tech tycoon.
item.content:encoded:
Prominent far-left figures, including livestream influencer Hasan Piker, are rallying around a pro-China media outlet within the sprawling network bankrolled by communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham – casting recent congressional subpoenas as leading a "McCarthy-style" witch hunt against the left.

As Fox News Digital first reported Wednesday, the House Ways and Means Committee sent subpoenas to three nonprofits, including media outlet BreakThrough News, as part of a wider investigation into alleged malign foreign influence by China in U.S. politics. The three groups have received about $39 million from Singham, who left the U.S. several years ago to live in China.

The other two groups are the People’s Forum Inc., a New York-based activist and political-education hub, and Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, a think tank that says its work is anchored in "national liberation Marxism."

The committee said it is examining whether nonprofit laws adequately protect against foreign influence and whether Congress needs to strengthen them. It also accused the three groups of failing to produce "a single responsive document" following earlier requests for information.

HOUSE PANEL SUBPOENAS 3 LEFT-WING GROUPS IN PROBE OF $39M TIED TO MARXIST TYCOON NEVILLE SINGHAM

Piker, CodePink rally behind subpoenaed outlet

Hours after Fox News Digital reported the subpoenas, pro-communist influencers and organizations mounted a social media defense of BreakThrough News, echoing similar-phrased attacks on the congressional investigation.

Among them were Piker, a prominent Twitch streamer and political commentator, and Medea Benjamin, co-founder of CodePink, a pro-communist, pro-China nonprofit that has received Singham money.

Piker called the subpoenas "the McCarthy trials," invoking the anti-communist Congressional investigations of the 1950s, led by Sen. Joe McCarthy.

"They will come for you," Piker warned on X.

Responding to BreakThrough News host Rania Khalek appeal for support and donations, Benjamin called the move a "terrible attack on independent journalism," adding, "We stand with you!!!"

Benjamin co-founded CodePink with Jodie Evans, who married Singham in 2017, the year he sold his technology company, ThoughtWorks, for an estimated $785 million. He has subsequently poured money into a network of pro-communist, pro-China organizations.

In March, Piker, Benjamin and Evans traveled to Cuba to rally support for the island nation’s communist government. Fox News Digital previously reported that the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control is investigating whether they violated U.S. sanctions restricting dealings with Cuba, according to sources familiar with the inquiry.

Their warnings about political repression come despite longstanding restrictions on dissent and independent media under the communist governments of Cuba and China.

The three organizations occupy different roles within the Singham network.

Breakthrough BT Media Inc., which runs BreakThrough News, is based at the People’s Forum W. 37th Street address in Manhattan. It serves as a propaganda arm of the network, producing media and protest coverage and "agitprop," or agitation propaganda. It’s often the first on the scene of major hotspots, like Glam Doll Donuts in Minneapolis, where a local activist, Alex Pretti, was killed by U.S. immigration agents earlier this year.

The People’s Forum organizes demonstrations and political programming, often the first to arrive at protests, handing out pre-printed signs from an affiliated group, the Party for Socialism and Liberation. Tricontinental, led by Singham friend Vijay Prashad, supplies Marxist research and ideological material and hosts events like a "Global South" conference last November in Shanghai, where Singham spoke, expressing support for the "new world order" of the Chinese Communist Party and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

GOP LAWMAKERS URGE TREASURY TO PRESS AHEAD WITH PROBE OF HASAN PIKER OVER CUBA TRIP

As Fox News Digital first reported, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York Jay Clayton from has separately launched a grand jury investigation into alleged wire fraud, bank fraud, money laundering and other financial improprieties by Singham in financing these organizations. Meanwhile, the State Department issued a report on Monday, naming People’s Forum and CodePink as "fellow travelers" in Cuba’s foreign influence campaign to sell communism.

The synchronized defense illustrates how organizations and personalities tied to the Singham network can rapidly mobilize around a common message, just as they’ve done in the past to oppose everything from data centers to President Donald Trump, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the war with Iran, Israel and the U.S. arrest of Venezuela strongman Nicholas Maduro.

Rather than addressing the committee’s allegations about foreign-linked funding, financial transparency and compliance with congressional document requests, many of the network’s most prominent voices characterized the investigation as political persecution, invoking themes of the "red scare," "McCarthyism," "censorship" and a broader "war on the left."

Messaging and fundraising push spreads

The wider campaign began Wednesday evening with a coordinated petition and fundraising push, before spreading through the Singham-linked network overnight and into today.

At 5:40 p.m. on Wednesday, the People’s Forum launched the messaging counterattack, sharing a new petition and a fundraising appeal on the platform Give Lively LLC, requesting tax-deductible donations to finance its legal response and "mass organizing work."

A few hours later, at 9:44 p.m, Khalek, the BreakThrough News host, urged her social media followers to "sign, share, donate" to the outlet’s new fundraising campaign on the GoFundMe platform and sign a petition, "Tell Congress: Drop the Witch Hunt Against BreakThrough News!"

The petition is hosted on Action Network, a big Democratic Party organizing platform. BreakThrough News said it sought "emergency funds to fight back."

"We’re not going anywhere," Khalek wrote on X. "We’re going to fight this assault on our journalism. The only rights we have are the ones we’re willing to defend."

According to Breakthrough BT Media’s tax filings, Khalek received $101,449 in 2024 and $108,160 in 2023 for "consulting."

Khalek hosts the outlet’s "Dispatches" program and co-hosts "The Freedom Side." Fox News Digital previously reported that she promoted the Chinese government’s claimed "eradication of extreme poverty" during a 2021 program with Tings Chak, a China-based researcher at Tricontinental, linking the media output of one subpoenaed organization to the ideological work of another.

WATCH: How funding from Marxist tycoon Neville Roy Singham flows to organizations

SINGHAM-BACKED, PRO-CHINA GROUP DROPS HUGE SUM ON MANHATTAN HQ AS FEDS PROBE SHADOWY NETWORK

About an hour later, at 10:52 p.m, Hartzell Gray, a congressional candidate in Missouri supported by Democratic Socialists of America and CodePink’s Benjamin, declared: "Truth isn’t partisan. Journalism isn’t a crime."

Soon after, at 11:45 p.m., Benjamin replied to Khalek, expressing her support, and at 11:51 p.m., Piker posted his condemnation of the subpoenas.

By 2:11 a.m. the next day, socialist congressional candidate Kshama Sawant, a former Seattle City councilwoman, shared Khalek’s message and told followers she had signed the petition supporting BreakThrough News. She described the subpoenas as a "shocking increase in repression of independent media and left activists."

Later that morning, at 9:34 a.m., the campaign had spread to propagandists for the Islamic Republic of Iran. Seyed Mohammad Marandi, a University of Tehran professor and former adviser to Iran’s nuclear negotiating team, shared BreakThrough News’ response and declared: "The US is an intolerant and authoritarian regime."

Marandi’s accusation comes against the backdrop of Iran’s own crackdown on dissent. A United Nations fact-finding mission said the Iranian government had intensified its repression in a "concerted effort to crush dissent," while Reporters Without Borders ranked Iran 177th out of 180 countries for press freedom in 2026.

About an hour later, at 10:39 a.m, Craig Mokhiber, a former senior U.N. human-rights official who previously directed the New York office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, called the subpoenas an "outrageous attack" by the "US-Israel Axis." He said they threatened freedom of opinion, expression and information.

Foreign-linked funding at heart of probe

At the heart of the committee’s inquiry is the network’s layered financial architecture.

The panel alleges that Singham’s money traveled through shell companies and donor-advised funds before reaching the three tax-exempt organizations. Such arrangements, the committee said, can move foreign-linked funding through layers of intermediaries that "by design, obscure the original source of the contribution."

Fox News Digital previously documented $278 million flowing from Singham into six core nonprofits in a wider transnational network spanning media operations, activist organizations and ideological think tanks. The committee’s current investigation focuses on about $39 million it says reached BreakThrough News, the People’s Forum and Tricontinental.

The committee requested records concerning foreign-linked funding and projects whose finances the groups managed. It also sought contracts involving foreign individuals or organizations, communications with Singham about the groups’ finances or operations, contacts with other foreign interests, information about foreign donors who contributed more than $5,000 and records of grants sent overseas.

By Thursday night, the counterpropaganda campaign went global with the World Socialist Website, a pro-communism platform, parroting the rhetoric of the Singham network and blasting the "anti-communist witchhunting" to its readers.

item.title: Eleven indicted in alleged Texas smuggling scheme that left 7 migrants dead in shipping container
item.description: Seven migrants died trapped inside a shipping container on a Union Pacific train in Texas, with a 14-year-old among the victims of the smuggling ring.
item.content:encoded:
Eleven people were indicted this week for allegedly participating in a years-long human smuggling operation that left seven illegal migrants dead in May after they were trapped for hours inside an unventilated shipping container in Texas.

Prosecutors say the migrants were loaded into the container near Del Rio before it was transported by train across the state. Six were later found dead inside it in Laredo and a seventh was discovered near railroad tracks at the San Antonio stop, according to authorities.

The victims — four Mexican nationals and three Honduran nationals — had no chance of escape because the container could not be opened from the inside, according to prosecutors.

"The ultimate destination for these aliens who began their journey in Del Rio was likely San Antonio. Once the train got to San Antonio, this alien smuggling organization that facilitated the movement of these individuals opened the train car doors," U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons said at a press conference on Friday.

SIX ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, INCLUDING 14-YEAR-OLD, FOUND DEAD IN SHIPPING CONTAINER ALONG SOUTHERN BORDER

"There was one individual inside that then fell out of the car. They left that individual for dead there by the tracks in San Antonio, closed the door to the container and sent the train on its way, the train ultimately ending up in Laredo, Texas, where the other six bodies were found," Simmons added.

One of the victims was a 14-year-old child, while another individual inside the car "frantically contacted their family as they were dying from the sweltering heat in that container," Simmons said.

The 11 defendants — four of them from the U.S. and seven from either Mexico, Honduras or Guatemala — allegedly ran a human smuggling organization from around April 2023 until May 2026, according to the indictment.

The group allegedly used cargo trains to get migrants further into the interior of the U.S. after getting them across the border, per the indictment.

MEXICAN NATIONAL SENTENCED IN BORDER CHILD SMUGGLING CASE INVOLVING THC-LACED CANDY

Prosecutors allege that toward the end of April this year, the organization began facilitating the travel of the group of seven migrants who would later die in the shipping container.

Each of the victims paid the smugglers between $1,500 and $10,000 to be transported from Acuña, Mexico, into the U.S., according to the indictment.

On the afternoon of May 9, the migrants made it into Del Rio, where the smugglers allegedly used a bolt cutter to snap the lock off a Conex shipping container that was aboard a stationary Union Pacific train, prosecutors said.

Once inside the container, the migrants were dealing with outside temperatures of 88 to 92 degrees Fahrenheit, according to investigators.

The train traveled along U.S. 90 to San Antonio, about 150 miles away from Del Rio, where the smugglers caught up with the migrants and found them "in peril," prosecutors said.

‘BAKED TO DEATH’: HOMAN RIPS MEDIA WHILE SHARING HORRIFIC SCENES FROM BORDER ENFORCEMENT CAREER

According to the indictment, the smugglers that were there allegedly left one of the migrants who had already died near the railroad tracks before abandoning the rest of the migrants inside the shipping container as it traveled to Laredo.

The next day, a worker at the Union Pacific Railyard in Laredo saw a leg sticking out of the container, leading to the discovery of the dead migrants, the indictment said.

San Antonio authorities later discovered the body of the migrant who had been left by the railroad tracks, prosecutors said.

Nine of the 11 people charged in connection with the smuggling and the deaths of the migrants have been arrested and are now in federal custody.

Mayra Alejandra Huerta, 32, of Del Rio, was the first to be arrested on May 12.

Last week, eight other defendants charged in the indictment were arrested in central and south Texas as part of a Homeland Security Task Force operation.

Those arrested from the U.S. were Edson Alejandro Perez, 18, of Del Rio; and Eric Hernandez, 40, of Eagle Pass, Texas.

Another two defendants arrested were from Honduras — Jonas Ulloa-Aguilera, 25, and Franklin Williams Ayala Aguilera, 30.

Three more were from Mexico — Maria Norma Neri de Moran, 56; Damian Huerta Analucas, 55; and Rosario Cristal Lopez-Saldana, 26.

Finally, Pascual Raymundo Loarca, 34, of Guatemala, was also arrested in the Homeland Security operation.

Two of those charged remain at large, including 37-year-old Karina Garcia of Del Rio and 35-year-old Seferino Huerta-Casillas of Mexico.

All the defendants were charged with one count of conspiracy to transport illegal aliens resulting in death and one count of aiding and abetting transport of illegal aliens resulting in death. They face a maximum of life in prison.

item.title: Measles surge hits new milestone as US cases surpass last year's total
item.description: U.S. measles cases in 2026 have officially surpassed 2025 totals, with 93% of patients unvaccinated or unknown for MMR as outbreaks persist.
item.content:encoded:
Measles has reemerged as a persistent public health challenge in the U.S. over the past two years — and the spread isn't slowing down.

According to a Johns Hopkins University tracker that compiles local and state health data, there were 2,295 confirmed measles cases in the U.S. as of July 22.

This figure has officially surpassed the 2025 numbers, which totaled 2,286 measles cases nationwide.

MEASLES-INFECTED TRAVELER MAY HAVE EXPOSED PASSENGERS AT LAX AND NEARBY HOTEL, HEALTH OFFICIALS WARN

Cases have been reported across the country, but concentrated outbreaks have worsened in some areas of Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Florida, Virginia, Utah, Texas and Arizona. In 2025, Texas had the largest outbreak, totaling 803 cases throughout the state.

In the latest CDC measles update on July 17, there were 34 new outbreaks reported in 2026, compared to 48 outbreaks in 2025. Most cases were associated with local outbreaks, while some were linked to international visitors.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Both this year and last year, 93% of all measles patients were either unvaccinated for measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), or had an unknown vaccination status, data shows.

Most cases have occurred in children and young adults between the ages of 5 and 19. There have been no deaths reported in 2026, according to the CDC, but there were three deaths in 2025.

The rise in cases comes more than two decades after health agencies reported that the disease was eliminated in 2000.

Measles can be spread through direct contact with infectious droplets, or can be airborne when an infected person breathes, coughs or sneezes, according to health officials. The virus can remain infectious in the air for up to two hours after an infected person leaves an area.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Symptoms usually appear within a week or two, and may include a high fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes.

A few days later, flat, red spots appear on the face and then spread down the neck to the rest of the body. People are most contagious in the four days before and four days after the rash appears.

Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst, emphasized the highly contagious nature of measles.

"Measles is so contagious that up to 90% of susceptible people who are exposed to an infected person will become infected," he told Fox News Digital, noting the importance of community protection. "We need a 95% vaccine coverage rate to ensure herd immunity," he said.

The herd immunity threshold is a mathematical estimate based on how contagious a disease is and how effectively immunity from vaccination or prior infection prevents its spread, according to Siegel.

"In this case, two-dose vaccination is almost 100% effective, and natural immunity after a measles infection is generally lifelong," the doctor said. "This isn’t about personal choice, it’s about community protection. We need to protect those who can’t have a live virus vaccine because they are immunocompromised or pregnant."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The doctor also cautioned that the U.S. could be at risk of losing its measles elimination status, as the number and duration of outbreaks suggest sustained local transmission within the U.S., rather than isolated cases linked only to international travel.

The CDC recommends that everyone receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, calling vaccination the best protection against measles.

Anyone who is showing measles symptoms or thinks they’ve been exposed should self-isolate and contact their doctor before showing up to a medical center and infecting others.

item.title: CBP intercepted biological materials tied to U.S.–China virus network before COVID, new documents show
item.description: Rand Paul reveals documents showing CBP intercepted undeclared biological materials tied to a U.S.-China coronavirus research network as early as 2018.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., has released another batch of documents related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The latest records show that U.S. officials intercepted undeclared biological materials tied to a U.S.–China coronavirus research network as early as 2018, likely in an attempt to avoid international tensions and regulatory scrutiny, Paul said.

The documents, which include a Department of Homeland Security intelligence report, primarily focus on a network centered around University of Minnesota virologist Fang Li.

SLACK MESSAGES RELEASED BY RAND PAUL APPEAR TO SHOW AUTHORS OF KEY COVID-19 ORIGIN PAPER HELD PRIVATE DOUBTS

In the years leading up to the pandemic, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) intercepted undeclared biological materials tied to this network of American and Chinese coronavirus researchers centered around Li, whose lab has been funded by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Paul stated in a news release.

In April 2018, Zhengli Shi, a scientist at the Wuhan Institute of Virology (WIV), asked Li to have a student transport antibodies for SARS research from the United States back to China.

Li told Shi that was not a good idea, given the "current tension between the USA and China," according to the documents. He suggested another scientist ship the antibodies instead.

CALIFORNIA MAYOR ACCUSED OF SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING PROPAGANDA WHILE IN OFFICE: FEDS

In October of that same year, Qibin Geng, a student in Fang Li's lab, offered to send live PEDV—a swine coronavirus—along with a growth protocol to Ralph Baric, a prominent American researcher.

Geng requested Baric's shipping address for the live virus. Geng had previously earned a degree from an institution affiliated with China's People's Liberation Army (PLA), but did not disclose any military service or affiliation on his visa application.

In November 2018, CBP agents at Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport intercepted three undeclared vials concealed in paper towels and wax film from a courier, who named Yusen Zhou of China's Academy of Military Medical Sciences (AMMS) as the source.

RAND PAUL BRINGS CIA WHISTLEBLOWER TO SENATE HEARING ALLEGING 'DEEP STATE' COVID-19 CONSPIRACY

In June 2021, the same courier was stopped again at the Detroit airport while traveling out of China, carrying 132 vials and a laptop belonging to someone else.

CBP reported that the vials likely contained a species of fly commonly used as a model organism in biological research. The courier was also carrying a laptop issued by a U.S. research institution to another individual, along with login credentials.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Li.

As Chairman of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Paul has released several batches of internal documents through his public archive, "The Reading Room."

Previous releases highlighted private doubts expressed by the authors of the "Proximal Origin" paper regarding the virus's source, as well as how the FBI halted a planned border inspection of another virus researcher.

item.description: Rahm Emanuel warned that socialist candidates force moderate Democrats in swing districts to answer for unpopular progressive positions ahead of midterms.
item.content:encoded:
Former Obama White House chief of staff Rahm Emanuel warned Thursday that "Bernie bros" and democratic socialist candidates could hurt the Democratic Party in November's midterm elections by forcing moderates in competitive districts to answer for unpopular progressive positions.

Emanuel wrote in a Wall Street Journal opinion column that Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) candidates could divert attention from the issue he believes Democrats should make central in the campaign.

"In the name of ‘authenticity,’ the DSA and others are saddling the Democratic Party with nominees whose wildly unpopular positions will protect Republicans from having to pay the price of Donald Trump’s corruption and economic incompetence," Emanuel said.

He compared the current political environment with 2006, when he led the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) as the party gained 31 House seats. He said Democrats succeeded by recruiting candidates who eased voters' concerns that the party was culturally out of touch and weak on national defense.

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS NEW GENERATION OF DEM SOCIALISTS DON'T LIKE AMERICA

The former Chicago mayor said efforts to elect socialists in safely Democratic districts have now created problems for candidates elsewhere.

"When the DSA attempts to turn safe Democratic states and districts a darker shade of blue, Democratic candidates in swing districts are put at a distinct disadvantage," Emanuel said.

Emanuel pointed to DSA member Darializa Avila Chevalier’s victory over Rep. Adriano Espaillat in New York’s 13th Congressional District. The Mamdani-backed candidate narrowly defeated the five-term incumbent and Congressional Hispanic Caucus chairman in June’s Democratic primary. Emanuel said Republicans could use the positions promoted by socialist candidates in heavily Democratic districts against moderates nationwide.

"What happens in the 13th District doesn’t stay in the 13th District," Emanuel said.

RISING SOCIALIST STARS ON TRACK TO CONGRESS: WHO ARE DARIALIZA AVILA CHEVALIER, BRAD LANDER AND CLAIRE VALDEZ?

Emanuel also blamed socialists for promoting positions that he said contributed to Democrats' recent electoral losses.

"It was socialists who led the charge to defund the police, open the borders, abolish prisons, release violent criminals onto the streets and degrade the flag," he said.

Emanuel cited Nebraska Democratic congressional nominee Denise Powell, whom the state Republican Party has labeled as "DSA Denise." Powell is running against Republican Omaha City Councilman Brinker Harding for an open seat in Nebraska's competitive 2nd Congressional District.

He argued that Powell should be able to focus on Harding's record instead of spending campaign resources separating herself from the socialist movement.

"Candidates in competitive districts have to spend time and effort differentiating themselves from the DSA’s agenda when they should be focusing voters on Mr. Trump’s corruption," Emanuel said.

He identified Powell as a "bright star perfectly positioned to flip" Nebraska’s 2nd Congressional District but said Republicans were unfairly labeling her.

Powell’s campaign denied any connection to the socialist organization in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Denise Powell is not a member of the DSA. She is a small business owner and working mom who is laser focused on lowering costs for Nebraskans and ending the rampant corruption in DC," campaign manager Ryan Longenecker said. 

On Tuesday, Emanuel got into a heated clash with The New Yorker's David Remnick over why the potential 2028 Democratic candidate wasn't emphasizing left-wing culture war topics like transgender issues. 

HOUSE REPUBLICANS AIM TO TURN DEMOCRATIC CIVIL WAR INTO MIDTERM WEAPON

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg was asked Friday on CNN's "The Situation Room" whether he agreed with Emanuel's argument. Buttigieg said moderate Democrats should focus on presenting their own agenda.

"Yeah, I think those of us who are more moderate in the party should concentrate our efforts on talking about what we’re for," he said. "Just like the Democratic Party as a whole has to be about more than just being against Republicans."

Buttigieg did not address Emanuel’s individual policy criticisms, instead promoting affordable healthcare, tax fairness and campaign finance reform.

"This is the kind of agenda that I think can be unifying, and I’m much more interested in that than any kind of factional project inside or outside the Democratic Party," Buttigieg said.

Buttigieg campaigned with Powell in Omaha earlier this month, WOWT reported. The DCCC has also placed Powell in its Red to Blue program, which supports Democratic candidates in competitive Republican-held districts.

A poll released Wednesday found Buttigieg in a close second to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in New Hampshire as a potential 2028 contender for the Democratic presidential nomination.

item.title: GOP rift grows as Thune hits brakes on Trump's election bill to avert shutdown
item.description: Sen. John Thune prioritizes a continuing resolution over the SAVE Act, sparking GOP tensions as Sen. John Kennedy warns against negotiating with Democrats.
item.content:encoded:
The wheels are in motion for Republicans to take another swing at President Donald Trump’s top election priority, but in the Senate, the main focus is keeping the government open.

House Republicans advanced their framework for another party-line budget reconciliation package that, among other funding priorities, includes a rough sketch to find a way to pass part of the SAVE America Act in the Senate.

But Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., is prioritizing another issue: preventing Senate Democrats from getting the opportunity to shut down the government ahead of the midterm elections in the fall.

JOHNSON DELIVERS BIG FOR TRUMP, BUT FRUSTRATION GROWS ACROSS RAZOR-THIN GOP MAJORITY

Thune plans to hold the House’s budget framework until the Senate can move a funding extension, known as a continuing resolution. Doing so, however, delays reconciliation, and in turn, trying to pass the SAVE America Act.

Negotiations on a continuing resolution between Republicans and Democrats are already underway in the Senate, but some in the GOP worry that Thune’s maneuver opens the door for betrayal.

"I support (Thune), I like him. I don't agree with him on this," Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., an appropriator, told Fox News Digital. "I've seen this vampire movie before. He wants to negotiate with the Democrats. I respect that, but right now, if you turn the other cheek to Chuck (Schumer), he’s just gonna stab me in the neck."

Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., told Fox News Digital she understood Kennedy’s position, but that Republicans needed to strike on funding the government while the opportunity was there.

"I believe that, particularly in the last year, we've seen Democrats getting more and more comfortable with not doing their job and finding a pathway forward," Britt said. "I do think we all have a duty and an obligation to try to find one here."

HOUSE GOP VOTES TO PUNT GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN BATTLE TO AFTER NOVEMBER MIDTERMS

Kennedy also is unhappy with the slowdown in passing the SAVE America Act, a sentiment shared by his colleagues in the House.

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., contended that the Senate could, and should, do both at the same time.

"Well, we all should be able to walk and chew gum at the same time," Scalise told Fox News Digital before the vote Tuesday. "In fact, this week, we're doing both. We're passing the reconciliation bill that will move SAVE America, and we're passing a continuing resolution to fund the government at current levels."

The House did pass a continuing resolution earlier in the week, but the Senate is working on a plan that could score Democratic votes, which, given the 60-vote filibuster threshold, is a necessity in the upper chamber.

House Appropriations Committee Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., told Fox News Digital he was largely open to whatever could help Republicans avoid a shutdown ahead of the all-important midterm elections.

"Obviously, we would consider anything they had," Cole said. "A lot depends on what's in it and whether or not, if we'd lost Republicans, are they going to replace them over here with Democrats? But no, I think the more talking about getting this done, the better off we are, the less chance of a shutdown."

Thune also floated attaching the continuing resolution to the reconciliation bill sent over by the House as a means of bypassing the 60-vote threshold, which Rep. Andrew Clyde, R-Ga., called "problematic" because they are two separate aspects of government funding that are not traditionally paired.

REPUBLICAN SAYS TRUMP'S TOP ELECTION PRIORITY 'DEAD' IN SENATE AS GOP FRACTURES AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

"I would suggest that Leader Thune do exactly what the House is doing," Clyde said. "Putting a continuing resolution on the budget reconciliation is problematic because you've got mandatory and discretionary funding mixed, literally for the entire Congress."

But the SAVE America Act may not even survive the strict rules that allow Republicans to use reconciliation. It also might not have the 50 votes needed to pass, either.

Thune, when asked about the criticism of his plan and the concerns holding up the SAVE America Act, told Fox News Digital, "as I've said before, we gotta get to 50."

"And I can't count to 50 right now on a budget resolution," Thune said. "But we'll see. I mean, we'll have those conversations at the conference. The priority is funding the government. And, so, to me, that's the thing we've got to keep our eyes on."

Republicans across the chambers agree on the latter point to find a way to keep the lights on and prevent yet another government shutdown.

But still, those not completely bought into Thune’s plan think that both issues can be completed.

"We need to do government funding, he’s right on that," Rep. Michael Cloud, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital. "We should also make sure our elections are secure, we should support the military, and so I think the reconciliation bill should move forward as well. But you know what, the Senate’s the Senate, they’ll do what they want to do."

item.title: Another top Seattle mayoral aide exits as Katie Wilson administration faces continued staff turnover
item.description: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson's press secretary is leaving City Hall after less than seven months, adding to significant staffing turnover in her office.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson's press secretary is leaving City Hall after less than seven months on the job, marking the latest high-profile departure from an administration that has already faced significant staffing turnover during its first year.

Local outlet PubliCola reported Wednesday that Sage Wilson made the call after "deciding he’d be more effective as an advocate for progressive causes outside the mayor’s office than inside it."

"Wilson, who previously worked in media relations for the labor advocacy group Working Washington and the progressive policy group Civic Ventures, doesn’t have a job lined up yet; his last day will be in early August," the report continued.

On his LinkedIn page, Wilson identifies himself as Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson’s deputy communications director.

SOCIALIST MAYOR KATIE WILSON SILENT AMID PROTESTS OVER ‘HUMAN DUMPING GROUND’ AHEAD OF US WORLD CUP MATCH

Sage Wilson's departure is the latest in a series of staffing changes inside Mayor Katie Wilson's office. PubliCola previously reported that the mayor's communications director, Seferiana Day, resigned in June after the mayor requested her resignation following several weeks of negative publicity.

According to the outlet, City Hall later brought in political consultant Crystal Nicole Fincher as a temporary communications advisor and Seattle Department of Transportation spokeswoman Dawn Schellenberg to assist with media relations.

On Thursday, the Everett Post reprinted a story from The Center Square that quoted Schellenberg as saying that the turnover is to be expected.

SEATTLE CLEANED UP FOR THE WORLD CUP BUT ONLY WHILE THE WORLD WAS WATCHING, COMMENTATOR SAYS

"It is common for new administrations to have some turnover and restructuring during the early phase as staff settle into their roles and address the priorities voters elected them to do," Schellenberg said.

Before taking office, Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson urged Seattle residents to boycott Starbucks in support of a baristas' union protest at one of the company's local stores. She later softened her stance after Starbucks announced it would establish a regional headquarters in Nashville and relocate some Seattle-based jobs there.

"I had the pleasure of visiting the Pike Place Market Starbucks a little while ago, and I ordered – I think it was a blueberry muffin latte that was like a staff creation," Wilson said during a June interview with FOX 13 Seattle co-anchor Hana Kim, who had asked Wilson if she still supports a boycott of Starbucks.

"I guess I broke my boycott," Wilson added. "And yeah, but I, you know, I don’t know. What do you want me to say about that?"

In a May Wall Street Journal opinion piece, former Starbucks CEO Howard Schultz criticized Wilson's "socialist rhetoric," arguing it reflected an anti-business climate contributing to companies leaving Seattle.

SEATTLE MAYOR’S STARBUCKS BOYCOTT CALL SLAMMED BY LOCAL RADIO HOST AS COFFEE GIANT ADDS NASHVILLE-BASED ROLES

"Seattle’s mayor, Katie Wilson, has chosen to cast business as a foil rather than a partner," Schultz wrote in the op-ed. "Her socialist rhetoric vilifies employers, even while she continues to rely on them for revenue. She has encouraged residents who disagree with her policies to leave."

News of Sage Wilson’s departure quickly prompted criticism from political opponents on social media, many of whom pointed to the administration's earlier staff changes as evidence of broader instability. Others wished the departing spokesman well and speculated about the demands of the job.

Fox News Digital reached out to Sage Wilson for comment.

item.title: 'America's Most Wanted' ex-cop fugitive returned after 20 years on the run to face murder, child sex charges
item.description: Dan Hiers, a former Charleston Police Department officer on the U.S. Marshals' 15 Most Wanted list, was returned from China after hiding for 20 years.
item.content:encoded:
A former South Carolina police officer accused of killing his wife before disappearing for more than two decades has been returned to the United States from China to face murder and child sex charges, the U.S. Marshals Service announced Thursday.

Dan Hiers Jr., 53, was taken into U.S. custody in Shanghai on Wednesday after deputy U.S. marshals traveled to China to escort him back to the United States.

Hiers is wanted in South Carolina on a Goose Creek warrant charging him with murder and a Dorchester County warrant charging him with criminal sexual conduct with a minor, the Marshals Service said.

MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE ON WEDDING NIGHT BROUGHT BACK TO US AFTER YEARS ON THE RUN IN MEXICO

Investigators allege Hiers shot his wife, 24-year-old Ludimila Hiers, in the back of the head while she slept inside the couple's Goose Creek home on March 15, 2005.

Authorities said the killing came just hours before Hiers was scheduled to surrender to face additional child sex charges in Dorchester County.

Dorchester County Sheriff Sam Richardson said his office has been notified that Hiers is being returned to face justice on the criminal sexual conduct with a minor charge filed in 2005.

"Daniel Hiers was entrusted to serve the public as a police officer. Instead, he is accused of betraying that trust and preying upon a child," Richardson said. "No badge, title, or position will ever place someone above the law."

Hiers, a former Charleston Police Department officer, had been suspended in 2004 after he was accused of sexually abusing a minor. He was arrested Nov. 24, 2004, on a charge of committing or attempting a lewd act upon a child under 16, according to South Carolina court records.

Additional charges were filed in March 2005, but Hiers failed to appear in court. The case has remained unresolved ever since.

The U.S. Marshals Service placed Hiers on its 15 Most Wanted list in June 2005, identifying him as one of the agency's highest-priority fugitives.

"Dan Hiers was in a position of public trust, but he betrayed that trust in the worst possible way," U.S. Marshals Director Gadyaces S. Serralta said in a statement. "Placing him on our 15 Most Wanted list made his capture a priority for this agency. His return to South Carolina is both significant and rewarding, and we thank our domestic and international partners for their tireless persistence in bringing this fugitive to justice."

A Marshals Service wanted poster described Hiers as "armed and dangerous" and noted he was a former police officer with 11 years of law enforcement experience who was trained in police tactics and martial arts.

The poster also said Hiers had allegedly stated he would not go to prison and might force an armed confrontation.

'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN

The Marshals Service said the operation to return Hiers involved China's Ministry of Public Security, the State Department's Diplomatic Security Service, the Justice Department's Office of International Affairs and the FBI.

Goose Creek police said Hiers' return marks the end of a decades-long effort to bring him back to South Carolina.

"The extradition of Dan Hiers means that justice can finally be served for the lives he destroyed," the Goose Creek Police Department said in a statement. "We are deeply appreciative of the U.S. Marshals Service for never wavering in its efforts to bring this fugitive back to the United States, and for keeping us updated over these long years of waiting."

"We also thank the State Department, Justice Department, and the FBI for their assistance," the department added. "We knew that there was a possibility Mr. Hiers would never be brought back to the U.S. — the fact that he has is a credit to the United States' commitment to justice."

The international operation also drew praise from the State Department's Diplomatic Security Service, which helped coordinate Hiers' return to the United States.

"The Diplomatic Security Service was proud to stand alongside the U.S. Marshals Service and our Chinese law enforcement counterparts to ensure Dan Hiers finally answers for his crimes," Nicholas Collura, principal deputy assistant secretary for diplomatic security and director of the Diplomatic Security Service, said in a statement.

Richardson also praised the federal agencies involved in securing Hiers' return from China, saying their "extraordinary collaboration ensured that a wanted fugitive who attempted to evade justice by fleeing overseas has been returned to face the criminal justice system."

The Hiers case was featured multiple times on "America's Most Wanted" and "The Hunt with John Walsh" as investigators searched for him over the past two decades.

It was not immediately clear when Hiers would make his first court appearance in South Carolina.

item.title: Shocking mid-flight brawl erupts after takeoff, sending flight back to airport
item.description: Approximately 10 passengers were reportedly involved in the brawl on easyJet flight EZY3352 from Tenerife to Liverpool, forcing the plane to turn back.
item.content:encoded:
A flight was forced to return to the airport after a passenger brawl erupted on board. 

The disturbing incident took place earlier this week on a flight from Tenerife, in the Canary Islands, en route to Liverpool, United Kingdom, the BBC and other outlets reported.

Approximately 10 passengers were involved in the brawl, which broke out on an easyJet flight soon after the flight departed, the outlet noted.

WHY A BLOWN-OUT PLANE WINDOW NEARLY SUCKED A PASSENGER OUTSIDE AT 16,000 FEET

Police met the 186-passenger aircraft upon its return, and the flight later continued to Liverpool.

An easyJet spokesperson confirmed the incident to Fox News Digital.

The official said the aircraft "returned to Tenerife South Airport after takeoff due to a group of passengers on board behaving disruptively."

The person added, "The flight then continued onto its final destination."

DELTA FLIGHT FORCED TO DIVERT AFTER PASSENGER GOES INTO LABOR AND DELIVERS BABY MIDAIR

The official added that easyJet's cabin and ground crews are trained to quickly assess and respond to on board disruptions to prevent passenger safety from being compromised.

"We take these incidents very seriously and do not tolerate disruptive behavior toward our staff," the spokesperson added.

"The safety and well-being of customers and crew is always our highest priority."

A spokesperson for the Civil Guard confirmed all the people involved were British nationals, according to Wales Online.

"Eight people were removed from the plane who had been traveling together, two adults and six minors. … [It appears] a heated discussion started in the airport terminal between two families before they boarded the plane, and those problems obviously continued on the plane, which is why it turned back," the spokesperson continued.

Commenters on an aviation-focused Reddit forum criticized the passengers for brawling aboard the flight.

"Of all the places, these people decide to fight inside the plane and during the flight," one person said.

Brits also poked fun at the flight's destination in Liverpool.

"Can’t be the Liverpool lads," another person said sarcastically. 

The easyJet incident is the latest in a string of recent passenger disruptions aboard airplanes.

item.title: Trump allies notch redistricting win as judges find no 'smoking gun' to scrap red state map
item.description: A three-judge panel ruled Tennessee's redrawn congressional map can stand for the Aug. 6 primary, rejecting claims it targeted Black voters in Memphis.
item.content:encoded:
A redrawn Tennessee congressional map expected to give Republicans a 9-0 advantage in congressional seats will remain in place for the state's Aug. 6 primary, handing President Donald Trump and his allies another victory as they work to preserve the GOP's House majority ahead of the midterm elections.

A three-judge panel on Thursday denied a request for a preliminary injunction filed by a group of Black Tennessee voters and civil rights organizations, who argued the map intentionally sought to weaken the power of Black voters.

The lawsuit stems from Tennessee lawmakers redrawing the state's congressional map during a special session in May after the Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, which made it harder to challenge redistricting plans on racial discrimination grounds. The new map split Memphis and Shelby County into three congressional districts, effectively dismantling Tennessee's only majority-Black district. Republican lawmakers said the goal was to create a map that favored Republicans in all nine congressional districts and help preserve the GOP's majority in the U.S. House of Representatives.

TENNESSEE PASSES NEW CONGRESSIONAL MAP LIKELY TO FLIP FINAL DEM SEAT AS PROTESTS ERUPT INSIDE CAPITOL

The judges — two Trump-appointed judges and one appointed by President Barack Obama — concluded the evidence pointed to partisan politics as the driving force behind the redistricting.

"At bottom, Plaintiffs won't succeed on their vote-dilution claim because they haven't presented meaningful evidence that race — not politics — motivated Tennessee's May 2026 map," the judges wrote.

The judges contrasted the case with the Supreme Court's 2017 decision in Cooper v. Harris, where the High Court ruled that there was direct evidence that race influenced the redistricting process.

SUPREME COURT RULES ON KEY VOTING RIGHTS ACT RULE AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS WAGE REDISTRICTING WAR

"Plaintiffs' evidence is a far cry from the 'smoking gun' direct evidence in Cooper v. Harris."

As evidence, the plaintiffs pointed to the map itself, which eliminates the state's only majority-minority district; lawmakers' use of census data containing racial demographics; the unusual timing of the mid-decade redistricting; Tennessee's history of racial discrimination; and affidavits from Black Memphis voters who said the new map diluted their voting strength.

"Plaintiffs present no direct evidence, weak circumstantial evidence, and no path for Tennessee to accomplish its political aims without producing the same effect," the judges wrote.

WHERE TRUMP, GOP VS DEMOCRATS REDISTRICTING BATTLE HEADS NEXT IN WAKE OF KEY COURT RULINGS

Amber Sherman, a plaintiff in the lawsuit and an affected voter, called the panel's rejection of the preliminary injunction "painful."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"The decisions by this court continue to further the disenfranchisement of Black voters in Memphis," Sherman said in a statement. "We deserve the same opportunity to shape our future as anyone else. When our voting power is diluted, our neighborhoods have a harder time making their voices heard on the issues that shape our daily lives."

While the preliminary injunction was denied, the lawsuit remains ongoing.

Since Trump began urging GOP-led states to pursue mid-decade redistricting, at least eight states have adopted new congressional maps, with Republicans hoping to gain seats in Texas, Florida, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Alabama, Louisiana and Tennessee. Democrats have responded with redistricting efforts in California, Utah and Virginia, although Virginia's new map was later struck down by the state's Supreme Court.
